verses.text: That same day, Jesus left the house and sat beside the sea.
Huge crowds gathered around him, so he got into a boat and sat down. Everyone else stood along the shore.
He taught them many things through stories. “Listen: a farmer went out to scatter seed.
“As he scattered it, some seed landed beside the road. Birds came and ate it up.
“Some landed on rocky ground with little soil. It sprouted fast because the soil wasn’t deep.
“But when the sun came up, it got scorched. With no roots, it dried up.
“Some seed landed among thorns. The thorns grew and choked it.
“Some landed in good soil and produced a harvest: one hundred times as much, some sixty, some thirty. 🌱
“If you have ears, listen!”
The disciples came and asked him, “Why do you teach them through stories?”
He answered, “You’ve been given the chance to understand Heaven’s Kingdom secrets; they haven’t.
“Whoever has will be given more, until they have plenty. But whoever doesn’t have, even what they have will be taken away.
“That’s why I teach them in stories: they look but don’t really see; they hear but don’t really listen or understand.
“Isaiah’s prophecy is coming true in them: ‘You’ll hear and hear, but never understand; you’ll look and look, but never see.

‘These people’s hearts have grown hard. Their ears barely hear, and they’ve shut their eyes. Otherwise, they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, turn back to me, and be healed.’
“But blessed are your eyes, because they see; blessed are your ears, because they hear.
“I’m telling you the truth: many prophets and righteous people wanted to see what you’re seeing but never saw it, and wanted to hear what you’re hearing but never heard it.
“So hear what the farmer’s story means.
“When someone hears the message about Heaven’s Kingdom but doesn’t understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was planted in their heart. That’s the seed beside the road.
“The seed on rocky ground is someone who hears the message and welcomes it right away, all excited,
“but they have no root and don’t last. When trouble or persecution comes because of the message, they stumble immediately.
“The seed among thorns is someone who hears the message, but worries about this age and the trickiness of wealth choke it. They become unfruitful.
“The seed in good soil is someone who hears and understands the message. They truly produce fruit: a hundred times, sixty, or thirty times what was planted.”
Jesus told them another story: “Heaven’s Kingdom is like a man who planted good seed in his field.
“While everyone was asleep, his enemy came, planted weeds among the wheat, and slipped away.
“When the green shoots came up and the grain formed, the weeds showed up too.
“The owner’s servants came and asked, ‘Sir, didn’t you plant good seed in your field? Where did these weeds come from?’
“He told them, ‘An enemy did this.’ The servants asked, ‘Do you want us to go pull the weeds?’
“‘No,’ he said. ‘If you pull the weeds, you might pull up the wheat with them.
“‘Let them grow together until harvest. At harvest time I’ll tell the reapers: First gather the weeds and tie them in bundles to burn; then bring the wheat into my barn.’”
He told them another story: “Heaven’s Kingdom is like a mustard seed a man took and planted in his field.
“It’s the smallest of seeds, but when it grows, it’s bigger than the garden plants and becomes a tree. Birds come and nest in its branches.”
He told them another story: “Heaven’s Kingdom is like yeast a woman mixed into three measures of flour, until all the dough rose.”
Jesus told the crowds all these things in stories. He didn’t say anything to them without a story,
to fulfill what the prophet had said: “I’ll speak in stories; I’ll reveal things hidden since the world began.”
Then Jesus sent the crowds away and went into a house. His disciples came to him: “Explain the story about the weeds in the field.”
He answered, “The one who plants the good seed is the Son of Man.
“The field is the world. The good seed means the children of Heaven’s Kingdom; the weeds mean the children of the evil one.
“The enemy who planted them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.
“Just as the weeds are gathered and burned, that’s what will happen at the end of this age.
“The Son of Man will send his angels to clear out everything that causes people to stumble and everyone who practices evil from his Kingdom.
“They’ll throw them into the fiery furnace, where people will weep and grind their teeth.
“Then the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father’s Kingdom. If you have ears, listen!
“Heaven’s Kingdom is also like treasure hidden in a field. A man found it and hid it again. Overjoyed, he sold everything he had and bought that field.
“Again, Heaven’s Kingdom is like a merchant searching for fine pearls.
“When he found one pearl of great value, he went and sold everything he had and bought it. 💎
“Again, Heaven’s Kingdom is like a net thrown into the sea that catches all kinds of fish.
“When it was full, the fishermen pulled it ashore. They sat down, put the good fish into containers, and threw away the bad ones.
“That’s how it will be at the end of the age. The angels will come and separate the wicked from the righteous,
“and throw them into the fiery furnace, where people will weep and grind their teeth.”
Jesus asked them, “Have you understood all this?” They answered, “Yes, Lord.”
He said, “So every teacher of the Law who becomes a disciple of Heaven’s Kingdom is like a homeowner bringing new and old treasures out of storage.”
When Jesus finished telling these stories, he left that place.
He went to his hometown and taught in their synagogue. The people were amazed: “Where did he get this wisdom and these miracles?
“Isn’t he the carpenter’s son? Isn’t his mother named Mary? Aren’t James, Joses, Simon, and Judas his brothers?
“And don’t all his sisters live here with us? Where did he get all this?”
They were offended by him. Jesus told them, “A prophet gets respect everywhere except in his hometown and his own house.”
He didn’t do many miracles there because they didn’t believe.
